QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_32

question.text: An AIF running an 'absolute-return' strategy typically benchmarks performance against:

answer.text: A fixed pre-determined rate set by the Investment Manager at scheme launch (e.g., 10% p.a.).
Realised equity risk premium of the prior 10 years.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 7.5: 'The benchmark for absolute-return strategies may be fixed rate, pre-determined by the Investment Manager at the time of launching the fund scheme, such as 10 percent per annum. Absolute Returns are not benchmarked against a broad-based market index or a relative benchmark.' Note: Cat I/II Managers rarely run pure absolute-return strategies (more common in Cat III) — but the PPM may still specify such a hurdle. **The Trap:** A and C are relative-return benchmarks — inapplicable to absolute-return strategies. D is a derived statistic, not a disclosed benchmark. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B Cat III Distributor exam leans heavily on absolute-return benchmarking. For XIX-D Cat I/II, the construct appears mainly for completeness. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If your Cat II fund has a hybrid mandate (some absolute-return sleeves), disclose the fixed-hurdle and the relative index benchmark for each sleeve in the PPM — hybrid disclosures reduce LP reporting-fit disputes.
